node.title: Re^3: Experimental push on scalar now forbidden
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I did a bit of digging in the archives. I believe the original proposal for autoderef is this: [https://rt.perl.org/Public/Bug/Display.html?id=78656|perl #78656: Allow push/pop/keys/etc to act on references] (this already contains a long discussion). The feature was [doc://perl5140delta#Array-and-hash-container-functions-accept-references|introduced in v5.14] (documented as experimental, but standardized warnings for experimental features weren't added until later, Update: [doc://perl5200delta#New-Warnings|in v5.20]).

This P5P thread appears to be one of the discussions about the problems with the feature: [http://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.perl5.porters/2011/08/msg175513.html|Bug in auto-dereferencing in 5.14?] My understanding is that there were lots of small problems with it, some philosophical but several practical, that added up to this being a contentious feature. Just to pick out two examples, again just based on my understanding from skimming the discussions: First, given that [doc://each], [doc://keys], and [doc://values] can operate on both hashes and arrays ([doc://perl5120delta#each,-keys,-values-are-now-more-flexible|since v5.12]), what does $x autovivify to in my $x; keys $x;? Second, what about [doc://bless]ed references that [doc://overload] their dereferencing operations?

Since part of the reasoning behind introducing autoderef was to make some expressions simpler (push @{$foo{bar}{quz}}, $x; became push $foo{bar}{quz}, $x;), i.e. getting rid of the need for circumfix @{} and %{} dereferencing, the [doc://perlref#Postfix-Dereference-Syntax] that was [doc://perl5200delta#Experimental-Postfix-Dereferencing|first introduced in v5.20] took care of that particular point (push @{$foo{bar}{quz}}, $x; became push $foo{bar}{quz}->@*, $x;). It seems to me that the discussion then generally moved in the direction that the problematic autoderef could be removed in favor of postfix deref (e.g. [https://rt.perl.org/Public/Bug/Display.html?id=119437|perl #119437: autoderef, the implicit deref in push REF and others], [http://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.perl5.porters/2013/11/msg209170.html|the future of auto-deref]), until that then [doc://perl5240delta#The-autoderef-feature-has-been-removed|happened in v5.24] together with postfix deref being taken out of experimental status as a replacement.

(Update: See also [doc://perlexperiment].)
